page: UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-2GB is an entry-level virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. This x86_64 architecture instance features a single shared vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 2.0 GB of system memory and 25 GB of local SSD storage. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single shared core delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests and high single-threaded throughput for gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, both ranking in the top 10%. However, due to the single-vCPU limitation, multi-core stress-ng performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also constrained, with PassMark memory scores in the bottom 10% and read-only memory bandwidth categorized as weak, though large-block write bandwidth remains average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that require high single-threaded burst performance but do not demand sustained multi-core execution or high memory density. The shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GB RAM capacity make it unsuitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale LLM inference, or heavy multi-threaded applications. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, simple automation scripts, and development or testing environments.
